questions.question: What was the primary purpose of the "Intensive Agricultural District Program (IADP)" launched during the Green Revolution in India?

questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Increasing agricultural productivity in specific districts**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Intensive Agricultural District Program (IADP)** was** launched in 1960-61** in India.
 
• It focused on the intensive use of inputs such as high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, chemical fertilizers, pesticides, and modern irrigation techniques.
 
• The program primarily focused on **wheat, rice, maize, and millet,** which were considered staple food grains in India.
 
• The IADP was launched by the Ministry of Agriculture during the **tenure of Jawaharlal Nehru as PM**. At the time, the **Agriculture Minister was S. K. Patil.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Initially, the program was introduced in 7 districts across various states that had high potential for agricultural production.
 
• These districts included: **West Godavari (Andhra Pradesh), Shahabad (Bihar), Raipur (Madhya Pradesh), Thanjavur (Tamil Nadu), Ludhiana (Punjab), Aligarh (Uttar Pradesh), and Pali (Rajasthan).**
 
• The** Green Revolution refers** to a period of significant agricultural transformation in India **during the 1960s and 1970s.**
 
• **In India**, **M. S. Swaminathan** is known as the **Father of the Green Revolution** for introducing these scientific agricultural practices to India.
 
• **Globally, Dr. Norman Borlaug**, an American agronomist, is regarded as the **father of the Green Revolution **for his pioneering work in developing high-yielding wheat varieties.
 
• The Green Revolution began in 1965, during the tenure of Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri, and continued into the early 1970s.
 
• The Green Revolution was **most successful in the Punjab, Haryana, and Western Uttar Pradesh**, where the required infrastructure, such as irrigation, was already well-developed.

__
 
• **e-NAM (National Agriculture Market)** is an online trading platform developed to create a unified national market for agricultural commodities.

• e-NAM was launched by the Government of India on **14th April 2016** as a major step towards agricultural reforms.
 
• The platform facilitates better price discovery through transparent auction processes and eliminates intermediaries, benefiting farmers directly.

• It comprises three components: **Price Support Scheme (PSS)**, **Price Deficiency Payment Scheme (PDPS)**, and **Pilot of Private Procurement and Stockist Scheme (PPPS)**.

• It replaced the earlier **MEIS (Merchandise Exports from India Scheme)** to align with World Trade Organization (WTO) rules.

questions.question: The mass of the body is halved and its speed is doubled. What happens to the kinetic energy of the body?
questions.solution:

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The energy which is possessed by an object due to its motion is called kinetic energy.**

 
 
• Kinetic energy, K.E. = 1over 2 mv², Where, m= mass of the object, v= velocity of the object.
 
 
 
• Now, as per given question, m₁ = 1over 2m, v₁ = 2v
 
 
• K.E.₁ = 1over 2m₁(v₁)² = 1over 2 x 1over 2m x (2v)² = 2 x1over 2 mv² = 2 K.E.
 
• **So that, K.E. is doubled.**

• **The total kinetic energy of an object depends on several factors such as the amount of work done on an object and its acceleration after a moment of inertia from external forces.**

 
 
• Kinetic energy is **directly proportional to mass as well as velocity.**
 
• K.E. is directly proportional to the** square of velocity, **therefore, changing the velocity will cause a greater change in kinetic energy. 
 
 
 
• There are three subcategories of kinetic energy: vibrational, rotational and translational.
 
 
• **Vibrational K.E. is caused by objects vibrating.**
 
• **Rotational K.E. is created by moving objects.**
 
• **Translational K.E. is caused by objects colliding with one another.**

questions.question: What does the term 'Automatic Route' imply in the context of Foreign Direct Investment (FDI)?

options.text: FDI that does not require prior government/RBI approval

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**FDI that does not require prior government/RBI approval**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Under the **Automatic Route**, foreign investors or companies can invest directly in India without seeking prior approval from the government or the Reserve Bank of India (RBI).
 
• This route applies to sectors where **100% FDI** is permitted without restrictions or specific conditions.
 
• The Automatic Route simplifies the FDI process, fostering a more **investment-friendly environment** for foreign entities.
 
• However, compliance with sector-specific regulations and adherence to the provisions of the **Foreign Exchange Management Act (FEMA), 1999**, are mandatory.
 
• The Automatic Route is regulated and monitored by the **Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade (DPIIT)**, ensuring transparency and efficiency in foreign investments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **FDI that requires Parliament approval**

 
 
• FDI does not directly require approval from Parliament for investments. Instead, specific policies and amendments related to FDI are discussed and passed in Parliament.
 
• Approval may be required for foreign investments in sensitive sectors such as defense, media, and atomic energy, where national interest is involved.
 
• Such investments are typically regulated under the **Government Route**, where prior approval from the concerned ministry or department is mandatory.
 
 
 
• **FDI that requires RBI approval**
 
 
• FDI requiring RBI approval generally falls under cases where investments do not comply with the provisions of the **Automatic Route**.
 
• For example, investments in prohibited sectors or those exceeding sectoral caps need explicit approval under the **Government Route**, which can involve RBI's consultation.
 
• RBI regulates foreign investments primarily through the provisions of FEMA and monitors compliance with foreign exchange-related laws.
 
 
 
• **FDI that is banned**
 
 
• FDI is prohibited in certain sectors under Indian regulations, such as:
 
 
• Lottery business
 
• Gambling and betting
 
• Chit funds
 
• Real estate business (except construction development projects)
 
• Manufacturing of tobacco and its substitutes
 
 
 
• Prohibition is enforced to safeguard national interests, social values, and public health.
 
 
 
• **Overview of FDI in India**
 
 
• Foreign Direct Investment (FDI) is a major driver of economic growth and an important source of non-debt financial resources for India's development.
 
• FDI policy in India is formulated by the **DPIIT**, which falls under the Ministry of Commerce and Industry.
 
• India permits FDI through two routes: the Automatic Route and the Government Route.
 
• The Government has liberalized FDI norms in various sectors to attract higher foreign investments, such as retail, defense, and insurance.

__
 
• Nutrients are the substances that are required by the organism/ plant to survive, grow, and reproduce.
 
• In the case of plants, different nutrients are absorbed by the roots and are then transported to the rest of the plant body.
 
• Xylem helps in the transportation of water, minerals, and nutrients in plants.

Explanation:__

An element is regarded as essential for a plant based on the following criteria:

 
• An element should be essential for the normal growth and reproduction of the plant.
 
• A requirement of an element should be such that it cannot be replaced by any other element.
 
• The element should be directly involved in the metabolism of the plant.

Based on the above-mentioned criteria and the quantitative requirements, nutrients are classified into two groups: Macronutrients and Micronutrients

Macronutrients:

 
• Macronutrients are needed in larger amounts by the plant tissues for their survival, growth, and other essential functions.
 
• Carbon (C), hydrogen (H), oxygen (O), nitrogen (N), phosphorus (P), sulfur (S), potassium (K), calcium (Ca), and magnesium (Mg) are the macronutrients required by plants.

Micronutrients:

 
• Micronutrients are needed in smaller amounts by the plant tissues.
 
• Micronutrients required by plants are iron (Fe), manganese (Mn), copper (Cu), molybdenum (Mo), zinc (Zn), boron (B), chlorine (Cl), and nickel (Ni).
 
• Apart from these essential elements mentioned above, elements such as sodium (Na), silicon (Si), cobalt (Co), and selenium (Se) are also required by some higher plants.

questions.question: In which type of geological formation are gorges most commonly developed?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Hard rocks**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Gorges are deep valleys with steep, almost vertical walls, commonly formed by the erosive action of rivers over geological time.
 
• They are most commonly developed in **hard rock formations** because these rocks resist erosion better than softer materials, allowing the river to cut deep, narrow valleys rather than wide ones.
 
• Examples of hard rocks where gorges are formed include granite, basalt, and other igneous or metamorphic rocks.
 
• Famous gorges like the Grand Canyon in the USA and Kali Gandaki Gorge in Nepal were carved through hard rock formations by persistent river erosion.
 
• The steep walls of gorges are created as the hard rock resists weathering and collapsing, maintaining the narrow and deep profile of the valley.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Soft sediment**:

 
 
• Soft sediment consists of loose, unconsolidated materials such as sand, silt, and clay, which are easily eroded by water and wind.
 
• In areas dominated by soft sediment, rivers typically form wide valleys or floodplains rather than narrow gorges.
 
• These areas are more prone to erosion and deposition processes, leading to the formation of features like meanders and oxbow lakes.
 
 
 
• **Glacial till**:
 
 
• Glacial till is an unsorted mixture of sediments deposited directly by glacier ice.
 
• It does not form gorges, as it lacks the structural integrity required to create steep walls.
 
• Instead, glacial till can form moraines, drumlins, and other glacial landforms.
 
 
 
• **Volcanic ash**:
 
 
• Volcanic ash consists of fine particles of volcanic glass and minerals ejected during volcanic eruptions.
 
• It is highly susceptible to erosion and compaction, making it unsuitable for gorge formation.
 
• However, volcanic activity can create other landforms, such as calderas, lava plateaus, and volcanic cones.
 
 
 
• **Gorge Formation**:
 
 
• Gorges are typically formed by the long-term erosive action of rivers cutting through resistant rock layers over millions of years.
 
• Other factors, such as tectonic uplift and changes in sea level, can enhance the formation of gorges by increasing river gradient and erosive power.
 
• Gorges can also be formed by glacial activity, where a glacier carves out a U-shaped valley that later becomes a gorge after glacial retreat.

• MFIs typically offer loans for income-generating activities, thereby helping borrowers to improve their livelihoods and escape poverty.

__
 
• The mitochondria are known as the powerhouses of the cell because they produce energy in the form of ATP through the process of oxidative phosphorylation.
 
• They contain their own DNA, which is separate from the nuclear DNA, and ribosomes, which allows them to synthesize some of their own proteins.
 
• Mitochondria are involved in various cellular processes, including the regulation of the cell cycle and cell growth.
 
• They are found in almost all eukaryotic cells, and their number can vary depending on the energy requirements of the cell.

• Rough ER is involved in protein synthesis and quality control, while Smooth ER is involved in lipid synthesis and detoxification processes.
 
 
 
• **Ribosomes**
 
 
• Ribosomes are the molecular machines responsible for protein synthesis in the cell.
 
• They can be found floating freely in the cytoplasm or attached to the Rough ER.
 
• Ribosomes are composed of RNA and proteins and are critical for translating mRNA into functional proteins.
 
 
 
• **Golgi Apparatus**
 
 
• The Golgi apparatus is a series of stacked membranes involved in modifying, sorting, and packaging proteins and lipids for secretion or delivery to other organelles.

questions.question:
Consider the following statements about glacial landforms:

**Statement 1: **Hanging valleys are often found opening into main glacial valleys at higher elevations.

**Statement 2:** Spurs of such hanging valleys are frequently truncated into triangular facets.

Which of the following Statements is/are **Correct**?
questions.solution:
The Correct answer is __**1 and 2 are correct**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Hanging valleys** are formed by tributary glaciers that join the main glacier at a higher elevation. This happens because the main glacier erodes deeper and more extensively than the tributary glacier.
 
• These valleys often open into **main glacial valleys** at a higher elevation, appearing as steep cliffs or waterfalls after the ice melts.
 
• The **spurs** of such hanging valleys are truncated into **triangular facets** due to glacial erosion. This truncation occurs as the glacier carves through the valley, cutting across the spurs and leaving behind triangular landforms.
 
• Hanging valleys are commonly associated with **waterfalls**, as the streams from the tributary valleys flow down into the main valley after the ice melts. A notable example is the **Yosemite Valley** in the United States.
 
• The processes involved in the formation of hanging valleys and triangular facets are examples of how glaciers reshape landscapes through both **erosion and deposition**.
 
• These features provide key evidence of the **intensity and direction of glacial movement** in an area, helping researchers understand past glacial environments.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Glacial Landforms**__

 
 
• Glaciers create various landforms through **erosion, transportation, and deposition**. These include features like cirques, horns, aretes, U-shaped valleys, and moraines.
 
• The study of glacial landforms helps in understanding **climatic changes** and the extent of glacial advances and retreats during the Earth's history.
 
• Glacial erosion processes like **plucking** and **abrasion** are responsible for the characteristic shape of valleys and other landforms.

__
 
• The **Iron Age** was marked by the widespread use of iron for tools and weapons, leading to advancements in agriculture, warfare, and urbanization.
 
• The **establishment of large cities** during this age was driven by the production of a **sizeable surplus** of agricultural products, which supported large populations and urban settlements.
 
• The **Painted Grey Ware (PGW)** ceramic is a significant archaeological marker of the Iron Age in the Indian subcontinent. This type of pottery is associated with the later Vedic period and reflects the cultural and economic activities of the time.
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization**, however, predates the Iron Age. It flourished during the Chalcolithic (Copper Age) and Bronze Age, making the third statement in the question incorrect.

 __

• It reflects the development of a settled agricultural society and the use of iron tools during the Iron Age.
 
 
 
• **Indus Valley Civilization**__
 __
 
• The **Indus Valley Civilization** existed during the Chalcolithic and Bronze Age, from approximately 2600 BCE to 1900 BCE.
 
• It was known for its advanced urban planning, drainage systems, and architecture.
 
• This civilization predates the Iron Age, which began around 1200 BCE in the Indian subcontinent.

• It led to significant advancements in **agriculture, warfare, and societal organization**.
 
• It saw the rise of early states and kingdoms, as well as the development of **trade networks**.

questions.question: Which of the following was NOT one of the factors leading to the economic reforms in 1991?

options.text: There was inflation in the economy.
There was a fall in India’s foreign reserves.
There was a rise in the fiscal deficit of the country.
There was stagflation in the economy.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**There was stagflation in the economy.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The 1991 economic reforms in India were a response to **several factors**, including:

 
 
• **Balance of payments crisis**:- India's foreign currency reserves fell to a low in 1990-91, making it difficult to pay for imports.
 
• **Inflation**:- The inflation rate increased from** 6.7% to 16.7%** as the money supply grew rapidly.
 
• Fiscal deficit:- The government's** fiscal deficit increased** due to increased non-development expenditures.
 
• **Iraq War**:- The Iraq war contributed to **higher oil prices **and the Gulf nations stopped sending foreign money to India.
 
• **Poor performance of public sector enterprises**:- The performance of public sector enterprises was poor due to political involvement. 
 
 
 
• In 1991, as India faced a severe economic crisis, that time:-
 
 
• Prime MInister: **P. V. Narasimha Rao**
 
• Finance Minister: Manmohan Singh
 
• RBI Governor: **S. Venkitaramanan**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Inflation**: A broad increase in the price of goods and services across an economy. A low and steady rate of inflation is considered a sign of a healthy economy. 
 
• **Deflation**: A period when prices fall, which can negatively impact an economy. Deflation can lead to a decrease in investments and production, which can increase unemployment. 
 
• **Stagflation**: A rare phenomenon that occurs when there is high inflation combined with weak economic growth and high unemployment. Stagflation can be difficult to recover from because policies that curb inflation can also curb growth. 
 
• **Disinflation**: A period when the inflation rate falls, but remains positive. 
 
• **Phillips curve**: A theory that describes the relationship between inflation and recession, which were considered mutually exclusive in the version of Keynesian macroeconomic theory that was dominant between the end of World War II and the late 1970s. 
 
• **Monetary policy**: Central banks use monetary policy tools like the bank rate, repo rate, and statutory liquidity rate to increase or decrease the money supply in an economy.

questions.question: The 16th Finance Commission (FC-16) has defined "Income Distance" based on which of the following calculations?

options.text: The difference between a state’s per capita GSDP and the state with the highest per capita GSDP.
The difference between a state’s per capita GSDP and the average per capita GSDP of all states.
The difference between a state’s per capita GSDP and the national average GDP per capita.
The difference between a state’s per capita GSDP and the average per capita GSDP of the top three large states with the highest per capita GSDP.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The difference between a state’s per capita GSDP and the average per capita GSDP of the top three large states with the highest per capita GSDP.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/7a63139f3b57ffe3814d27f8dcaee8cb420142f7146b480d479d526074519671.png] **__In News__**

__
 
• **The 16th Finance Commission (FC-16) introduced a refined definition for 'Income Distance' to determine horizontal devolution for 2026-31.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **Key Points__**

__
 
• **Income distance is now calculated as the gap between a state's per capita GSDP and the average of the top three large states with the highest per capita GSDP.**
 
• The Per capita GSDP is computed as the average over the period 2018-19 to 2023-24.
 
• To ensure data accuracy and fairness, the pandemic year of 2020-21 has been excluded from this average calculation.
 
• States with a lower per capita GSDP receive a higher share under this parameter to promote fiscal equity across the country.
 
• Income Distance Statistics:__
 __
 
• Weightage in FC-16 - 42.5%
 
• Calculation Period - 2018-19 to 2023-24 (Excluding 2020-21)
 
• Benchmark - Average of top 3 large states
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• GSDP (Gross State Domestic Product)__

 __
 
• It represents the total value of all finished goods and services produced within a state's borders during a specific period.
 
 
 
• Equity vs. Efficiency__
 __
 
• Income Distance is an 'equity' parameter (helping poorer states), while the new 'Contribution to GDP' is an 'efficiency' parameter (rewarding productive states).
 
 
 
• 15th FC Comparison__
 __
 
• The 15th FC typically used the distance from the single highest-income state, whereas the 16th FC uses an average of the top three to create a more stable benchmark.
 
 
 
• Horizontal Devolution__
 
 
• The allocation of the 41% tax pool among states based on the formula containing Income Distance, Population, Area, etc.

• The Constitution initially allowed English to continue as an official language of the Union for a period of 15 years from the commencement of the Constitution (1950), which was later extended through amendments.

questions.question: The ratio of the present ages of Ram and Ramesh is 3 : 5. After 7 years the ratio of their ages will be 4 : 5. Find the present age of Ramesh.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Present ratio of **Ram** and **Ramesh** = 3 : 5 (Difference = 2 units).

Ratio after **7 years** = 4 : 5 (Difference = 1 unit).

To equate differences, multiply the future ratio by 2: (4 : 5) × 2 = 8 : 10.

Change in **Ramesh’s** age units = 10 − 5 = 5 units.

Given that 5 units = **7 years**, then **Ramesh’s present age** (5 units) is 7 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 years.**

**__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Present age ratio of **Ram** and **Ramesh** = 3 : 5

Ratio after **7 years** = 4 : 5

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/1161eea55afb5292cf1f5777e68fde8e608e6f90bd94cbcb9663c234c6b05b77.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the present ages of **Ram** and **Ramesh** be 3x and 5x respectively.

⇒ After **7 years**, their ages will be (3x + 7) and (5x + 7).

⇒ According to the problem: (3x + 7) ÷ (5x + 7) = 4 ÷ 5

⇒ 5 × (3x + 7) = 4 × (5x + 7)

⇒ 15x + 35 = 20x + 28

⇒ 20x − 15x = 35 − 28

⇒ 5x = 7

⇒ **Ramesh’s present age** = 5x = 7 years.

**∴ The correct answer is 7 years.**

**__Additional Information__**

Age Difference Consistency

The difference between the ages of two individuals remains **constant** throughout their lives. If the difference is 'd' now, it will remain 'd' after any number of years.

Ratio Adjustment Method

When the time gap is the same for both people, adjust the ratios such that the **numerical difference** between the terms of each ratio is identical.

Cross-Multiplication in Ratios

For a ratio a : b changing to c : d after 'n' years, the value of one part x = [n × (d − c)] ÷ [ad − bc].

questions.question: The base of a pyramid is rectangular whose breadth and length are in the ratio 4 : 7, the volume is 112000 cm³ and the diagonal of the base is 10√65 cm, then find the height.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Ratio of **Diagonal** = √(4² + 7²) = √65 units.

Scale factor = Actual **Diagonal** ÷ Ratio **Diagonal** = 10√65 ÷ √65 = 10.

Base **Breadth** = 4 × 10 = 40 cm and **Length** = 7 × 10 = 70 cm.

**Base Area** = 40 × 70 = 2800 cm².

**Height** = (3 × **Volume**) ÷ **Base Area** = (3 × 112000) ÷ 2800 = 120 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

⇒ Ratio of **Breadth** to **Length** = 4 : 7

⇒ **Volume** of the pyramid = 112,000 cm³

⇒ **Diagonal** of the base = 10√65 cm

**Formula Used:**

⇒ **Diagonal** of rectangle = √(Length² + Breadth²)

⇒ **Volume** of pyramid = (1/3) × **Base Area** × **Height**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/9d9f5dc8ee5492670c8eed49b4cea0f12a03b3470e910948fb5d54fc7686b696.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the **Breadth** (B) = 4x and **Length** (L) = 7x.

⇒ (10√65)² = (7x)² + (4x)²

⇒ 100 × 65 = 49x² + 16x²

⇒ 6500 = 65x²

⇒ x² = 100 ⇒ x = 10 cm.

⇒ **Length** (L) = 7 × 10 = 70 cm and **Breadth** (B) = 4 × 10 = 40 cm.

⇒ **Base Area** = 70 × 40 = 2800 cm².

⇒ 112000 = (1/3) × 2800 × **Height**

⇒ 112000 = (2800/3) × **Height**

⇒ **Height** = (112000 × 3) ÷ 2800

⇒ **Height** = 40 × 3 = 120 cm.

**∴ The correct answer is 120 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**
